findings.title: Two artefact schemas were closed (additionalProperties widened to strict $ref) and shipped as MINOR, contradicting §5.5's own MAJOR rule for schema changes
findings.before: schema/managed.schema.json (base): "files": { "additionalProperties": true, "required": [], "properties": {}, "type": "object" } — any shape was accepted per file entry. schema/tally.schema.json (base) per_id: "additionalProperties": true, "required": [], "properties": {}.
findings.after: schema/managed.schema.json (head): "files": { "additionalProperties": { "$ref": "#/$defs/entry" }, ... } where entry now requires template, version, sha256 with additionalProperties: false. schema/tally.schema.json (head) per_id: "additionalProperties": { "$ref": "#/$defs/entry" } where entry requires act, act_demoted, state, closed_by with additionalProperties: false and closed enums on act/state/closed_by. Sync.jl's own updated docstring: "the schema closed its files map after a release that never validated it, so a sidecar an older copy wrote can fail here", and its updated error message appends: "a sidecar written before its schema was closed; delete it and re-run gbg sync". The CHANGELOG's own Unreleased entry says: "Three JSON schemas were tightened in a commit whose message did not name them: managed and tally closed their per-entry maps... The last was reverted... the other two stand," while the same section is still headed "MINOR so far."
findings.why_it_matters: §5.5 states without qualification: "Every verdict vocabulary and schema... Changing any vocabulary is MAJOR." This diff changes two schemas from open to closed unions and, by the tool's own docstring and changelog, this REJECTS a .gbg/managed.json sidecar that a previous (older) release of the very same tool wrote and that validated fine before — exactly the "reject usage that used to work" pattern the audit is watching for. It is bundled into a release still marked MINOR, and the changelog itself flags that the underlying commit did not even name the schemas it tightened. Any consumer (including the tool's own self-consumption, D15) upgrading past this point can have gbg sync throw a SyncError on a sidecar it wrote itself under the prior schema, and a mid-round Passes.grade that carries a prior pass's per_id entry forward (Passes.jl's new scope-narrowing) risks the same for tally.json written by an earlier pass under the old, looser per-entry schema.
findings.description: The underlying motivation (closing an unvalidated map so a malformed sidecar/tally entry is caught rather than silently accepted) is reasonable, but the package's own written invariant classifies any schema change as MAJOR, and this diff both under-declares the severity (MINOR) and, by its own admission, did not disclose the schema tightening in the responsible commit message. The fix is real but the compatibility break for pre-existing artefacts is not scoped or announced to match the package's own rule for this exact kind of change.
findings.evidence: "Three JSON schemas were tightened in a commit whose message did not name them: managed and tally closed their per-entry maps... the other two stand, and a sidecar an older copy wrote now names itself in the refusal." (CHANGELOG.md, Unreleased) together with "MINOR so far." in the same section, and Sync.jl's own "a sidecar an older copy wrote can fail here."

findings.title: TestHarness.resolve_function's module search order was reversed (externals now searched last, not first), silently changing which module 'owns' a name-colliding method for method_parity counting fleet-wide
findings.before: function resolve_function(name::Symbol, pkg::Module, modules::AbstractVector{Module}; externals = (Base,)) searched Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules)) — i.e. Base (or whatever externals names) was checked before the package's own owned modules.
findings.after: The same function now searches Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals)) — the package's own modules are checked before externals. The updated docstring explains: "searched LAST so a package function always wins its own name (Config.read, Git.run and Scan.report all share one with a Base export, and Base ahead of them handed the caller the wrong generic)."
findings.why_it_matters: resolve_function feeds module_method_count/method_parity, the frozen-baseline test-harness contract (test/method_parity_baseline.toml) shared by all four GBG consumer packages. For any package operation whose name collides with a Base export, this reverses which module's method count the operation is attributed to. A consumer whose baseline was authored (and passing) under the old resolution order can now see its counts shift between the package module and Base after adopting this tool version, breaking Pkg.test() for a baseline that was previously valid and unchanged.
findings.description: This appears to be a genuine, well-motivated bug fix (the tool's own operations were being misattributed to Base), and it is the correct behavior a reader of module_method_count's docstring would expect. It is not disclosed in the CHANGELOG's Unreleased section at all, unlike the schema tightening above, even though it is a fleet-wide, silently-behavior-changing edit to a frozen-baseline harness contract that every consumer inherits on bump.
findings.evidence: for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules)) (base) vs for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals)) (head), src/TestHarness.jl, resolve_function.
